transcription.text: That's exactly how millions of adults are going to feel on November 19th when they played GTA 6 for the first time.
GTA 6 took 13 years and 2 billion dollars to make.
The release got pushed from 2025 to May 2026, and then again to November.
And yet, nobody seems to have moved on.
But why?
Why are grown adults waiting 13 years for a game that's supposedly just about stealing cars?
Because GTA was never just about cars and guns.
It was about what it really gave you.
Freedom.
Back to being 10 years old, sitting in front of the family computer, playing Vice City with the volume turned all the way down so nobody could hear the gunshots.
With cheat codes like Aspirin and Panzer scribbled at the back of your notebook.
For a kid, it wasn't just a game.
It was a psychological escape.
An alternate reality.
It was everything you imagined adulthood would be.
Driving supercars, firing guns, flying planes, and owning an entire city.
And while every other game asks you to be the hero, but GTA lets you be the problem.
It lets you be the bad guy in a world that looks just like yours.
And somewhere along the way, those kids grew up.
Today, it's the exact opposite.
It's an escape from adulthood, back to the world they once dreamed of living in.
And on November 19th, Rockstar takes you back to Vice City, the city where it all started.
So if you're still lost in Los Santos this week, don't rush.
Take the long way home. Drive slow.
Because that 10-year-old playing GTA Vice City never really left.
He's just been waiting 13 years to feel that freedom again.
